model_annotation:
The diagram depicts the ex- and imports of goods as well as the trade balance surplus/deficit in the USA. The x-axis is labeled with years from 1995 to 2025, with a linear scale and interval of five years, marked in equal intervals. The y-axis is labeled in millions of US dollars, ranging from -200 to 400, with a linear scale and intervals of 50. 

The diagram displays three lines: one blue line representing the trade balance, one purple line representing exports, and one light blue line representing imports. The trade balance line starts at approximately -30 in 1995, fluctuates and increases to around 60 in 2000, decreases to around -70 in 2009, and then increases to approximately 60 in 2020 and is projected to increase to 90 in 2025. The exports line begins at around 95 in 1995, increases to approximately 130 in 2000, decreases to 90 in 2009, and then increases to 250 in 2020 and to approximately 270 in 2025. The imports line starts at around 130 in 1995, increases to 150 in 2000, decreases to 120 in 2009, and then increases to 190 in 2020 and to approximately 180 in 2025.
